s1.syndrome_frame: Acute monoarticular joint pain and swelling with a mass
salient_findings: Right knee pain and increased back pain
5 × 10 cm soft, fluctuant, non-tender mass in the posterior aspect of the right knee
Moderate to large joint effusion without definite synovial thickening
key_facts: History of lung cancer with bone metastases

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute monoarticular joint pain and swelling with a mass
salient_findings: Right knee pain and increased back pain
5 × 10 cm soft, fluctuant, non-tender mass in the posterior aspect of the right knee
Moderate to large joint effusion without definite synovial thickening
key_facts: History of lung cancer with bone metastases

differentials: Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath
per_call: Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath

shortlist.label: Septic arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of recent joint aspiration and a mass in the posterior aspect of the right knee, which could be indicative of an infectious process

shortlist.label: Brucellar arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of treated brucellosis 5 years earlier, which could be a rare but plausible cause of the current joint symptoms

shortlist.label: Pseudogout
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of osteoarthritis and the presence of a joint effusion, which could be consistent with pseudogout

shortlist.label: Gout
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of joint pain and swelling, which could be consistent with gout, although the absence of erythema and warmth makes it less likely

shortlist.label: Osteoarthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of bilateral knee osteoarthritis, which could be contributing to the current joint symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a soft, fluctuant, non-tender mass in the posterior aspect of the right knee with a moderate to large joint effusion and absence of fever or elevated white-cell count is more consistent with pseudogout, which is often seen in older adults with a history of osteoarthritis and can cause joint effusions without significant signs of infection.

rejected.label: Septic arthritis
rejected.why: The patient is afebrile, has a low white-cell count, and lacks signs of infection such as erythema, warmth, or discharge, making septic arthritis less likely.

rejected.label: Brucellar arthritis
rejected.why: Although the patient was treated for brucellosis 5 years earlier, the current presentation does not strongly suggest an active brucellosis infection, and the time frame since treatment makes reactivation less likely.

rejected.label: Gout
rejected.why: Gout typically presents with acute, intense pain, swelling, and erythema, which is not consistent with the patient's non-tender mass and lack of significant signs of inflammation.

rejected.label: Osteoarthritis
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of osteoarthritis, the acute presentation of a large joint effusion and a soft, fluctuant mass suggests a more acute process superimposed on the chronic condition, such as pseudogout.
